appearsIn: js/effects.js:174-189 (inside drawAoeImpacts)
currentState: Radiating kinked fissure lines that sell the blast as something that happened on the floor. Count is 7 rays, dropping to 3 when the kind contains "hit". Angles are fully deterministic from the impact's seed: angle = (seed % 17)*0.11 + ray*2*PI/rays, so an impact never flickers between frames. reach = front * (0.5 + (ray%3)*0.13) gives three interleaved lengths (0.50, 0.63, 0.76 of the current ring radius), and because `front` grows the rays lengthen with the ring. Each ray is a two-segment polyline with a 0.16 rad kink: moveTo(impact.x, impact.y), lineTo at 0.52*reach along `angle`, then lineTo at full reach along angle+0.16 — with every y component multiplied by Visuals3Q.GROUND_SQUASH (0.56) so the rays lie in the projected ground plane. ctx.lineCap = "round", lineWidth = Math.max(0.8, 2.2*fade) tapering 2.2 px -> 0.8 px, stroke rgba(rgb, 0.5*fade) in the same orange/violet as the ring. Note ctx.lineCap is set here and never restored, so it leaks "round" onto whatever draws next in the world layer.

appearsIn: js/gl/gl-geometry.js:143-161 (offset/mitre solver)
currentState: Corner treatment for the ribbon. Each polyline vertex gets ONE shared offset direction (the normalized sum of the two segment perpendiculars) scaled by 1/cos(half-angle), clamped: scale = min(2.5, 1 / max(0.35, dot)). End vertices use their single segment's perpendicular. Result: continuous ribbon with no wedge gaps on the outside of a bend, and hairpins produce a blunt truncated corner rather than a spike. Corners are hard-edged - no rounding, no fillet, and no extra tessellation, so a 90-degree turn (rune-circuit, mana-coil) is a single sharp mitre and the sigil-lattice switchbacks are sharp obtuse mitres.

currentState: anchorWorld applies the same yaw-and-uniform-scale matrix drawActor used: x = tower.x + (cos·pt0 - sin·pt1)·k, y = tower.y + (sin·pt0 + cos·pt1)·k, z = pt2·k, with k = GLModels.unitsToPx("sniper-base") (fallback 31.8032) and yaw taken from tower.aim — deliberately not core.aimRad, because the body on screen tracks its target inside the arc and reading the player's chosen angle would float the light off the barrel. Reuses a single mutable scratch object. barrelAxis derives the weapon's on-screen unit direction from two projected anchors rather than from the aim angle, since under a turning camera the two are not the same, and returns { x, y, len, scale } or null when the two points collapse.

currentState: One shared particle type backs every burst in the game. spawnParticle(x,y,color,speed,size,life) picks a uniform random angle 0..2*PI, sets v = speed*(0.35 + Math.random()*0.65) (so 35-100% of the nominal speed), and jitters size to size*(0.6 + Math.random()*0.8) (60-140%). Colour is carried as a bare "r,g,b" byte-triplet string, never a CSS colour. Integration is Euler at the fixed 1/60 s step: x += vx*dt, y += vy*dt, then vx *= 1 - 3*dt and vy *= 1 - 3*dt — an exponential drag of e^(-3t), i.e. velocity down to ~5% by 1.0 s, which is the "bloom and settle" curve. No gravity, no arc, no rotation, no collision, no additive blending. Drawn as a single flat filled ctx.arc of radius p.size * a where a = life/maxLife, filled rgba(color, 0.85*a) — so both radius and alpha decay strictly LINEARLY to zero, no easing. Hard cap MAX_PARTICLES = 400, enforced FIFO by particles.shift() at spawn time (oldest silently dropped). Array is handed out unwrapped by worldState() for the 3D renderer, which re-projects the same objects with a parabolic altitude arc (h = 46t - 78t^2) and streak geometry instead of dots (js/gl/gl-world.js:1434-1462).

currentState: Pure Lambert diffuse, two directional terms plus a constant ambient, evaluated per fragment on the interpolated normal: n = normalize(vNrm); key = max(dot(n,uKeyDir),0.0) * uKeyStrength; fill = max(dot(n,uFillDir),0.0); lit = vCol * (uAmbient + vec3(key) + uFillColor * fill). There is NO specular term of any kind - no half-vector, no view direction, no Blinn/Phong exponent, no fresnel, no rim term; the fragment shader never receives or computes a view vector. There is no shadowing, no ambient occlusion, no normal mapping. Faceting comes entirely from geometry (per-triangle normals duplicated across the 3 vertices), not from a second shading path.

currentState: Three implementations of the same exact piecewise sRGB EOTF, kept deliberately identical: f <= 0.04045 ? f/12.92 : ((f+0.055)/1.055)^2.4. GLGeometry.hex() parses '#rgb' or '#rrggbb' (expanding 3-digit form), splits the int into bytes and runs the curve, returning a linear [r,g,b]. appearsIn: js/visual-models.js:22-105 — the seam every skin in the game passes through
currentState: Seven categories (tower, enemy, summon, projectile, map, effect, ui). renderer(category,id) falls back to the category-wide '*' entry. draw() returns false when there is no model OR when the model itself returns false, which is what makes lazy sheet loading invisible. Id conventions: ':body' replaces only the skin and keeps bars/ranges/abilities; ':complete' replaces the whole renderer; ':icon' the build-bar art. install() takes a whole pack object. Models receive live objects and must treat them read-only.

appearsIn: js/game.js:2751-2769 (draw dispatch); setters at js/game.js:1282-1300 (openMapSelect/openMenu/leaveRun), js/store.js:60-64 (Store.open), js/codex.js:232-242 (Codex.open)
currentState: There is NO transition. Screen changes are a bare assignment to the `screen` global, and draw() branches on it the very next frame: menu, select, index and store each early-return after painting their own opaque background, and play clears to the map's background colour. No crossfade, no wipe, no loading state, no camera move — one frame is the old screen and the next is the new one. Codex.open() and Store.open() rebuild their models on entry (thirty-odd throwaway tower/enemy instances for the index), which is the only cost of the change.
